I’ll inspect the failed corpus gate’s retained summary and the phase’s bead notes first, then continue with the visual review and remaining checks from the checkpoint.

The release build succeeded, and the corpus run produced its PDFs/pages before failing. I’m narrowing down the gate’s actual failure from its summary and retained logs, then I’ll inspect the requested pages against the visual criteria.

The failure is in the gate script, not rendering: the final dry run hit `vault_basename_counts: bad array subscript` while checking an empty basename. I also found the corpus summary still reports nine raw block-ID labels, so I’m tracing both findings before deciding whether the ownership is in the script or the link-label code.

I’m using the SASE artifact and monitor workflows now: the parent plan is stored as an audited artifact, and the next full corpus run may take long enough to hand to the monitor.

The visual review shows the status glyphs, task text, and compact Scheduled rows are on the intended lines, and the cash page has the `AREA` kicker. The gate’s extra findings point to two more issues: generic file embeds (especially schedule-log files) still warn as missing, and its raw-ID scan is counting Markdown link destinations as visible labels. I’m reproducing those with synthetic cases and will also make the sweep handle an already-captured same-day snapshot.

The synthetic regression tests exposed one more detail: the attachment index was refusing path misses as intended by an old guard, but its basename fallback was still looking up the whole path. I’ve changed the fallback to use the final filename and am formatting before rerunning the focused snapshot tests.

The new synthetic tests cover block-embed labels, generic file links, and unique-basename fallback; the first run found and corrected an outdated expected label. I’m checking one layout issue from the page review before the rebuilt binary and corpus rerun.

The inspected pages also showed the Scheduled lane title stranded at the bottom of page 1 while its date group starts on page 2. I’ve added a synthetic layout guard so that title reserves enough room to stay with its first group. The focused Pandoc layout test passes; I’m handing off the release rebuild, then the synthetic smoke and final athena gate.
